name: How Bridges, Canals and Rails Shrank the World
description: The roads, canals, tunnels and railways that cut journeys from months to days, and the engineers who bet fortunes on them.

checkpoints.name: Roads and waterways of empire
checkpoints.note: Rome paved its roads and carried water over valleys on arches, while Chinese rulers dug a canal to link their river basins. Caravans on the Silk Road tied distant empires together.

checkpoints.name: Stone bridges and early canals
checkpoints.note: Ottoman builders threw an arch across the Neretva at Mostar, Inca engineers strung rope bridges and roads over the Andes, and French engineers dug a canal to link two seas.

checkpoints.name: Iron, steam and canals
checkpoints.note: The Industrial Revolution brought cast iron, locomotives and canal booms. The first iron bridge, the first steam railway between two cities and the first tunnel under a river all appeared within about sixty years.

checkpoints.name: Continents connected
checkpoints.note: Rails crossed America and Siberia, the Suez Canal joined two seas, and the Panama Canal cut through a continent. Steel bridges in New York, Scotland and London became wonders of the age.

checkpoints.name: Modern megaprojects
checkpoints.note: Concrete dams, deep tunnels and record-length bridges tied nations together. Highways like Route 66 changed travel, and long tunnels now link islands and mountain regions.
